administered_by: the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, through three managed care organizations covering five CHC zones
eligibility_threshold: Pennsylvania does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. CHC is for people 21 and older who either have both Medicare and Medicaid, receive Medicaid long-term services and supports, or live in a Medicaid-funded nursing home. Clinical eligibility rests on needing help with everyday personal tasks at a nursing-facility level of care.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the state CHC program page; set by Pennsylvania Medicaid financial eligibility rules
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the state CHC program page; spousal impoverishment rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the state CHC program page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: Apply online through COMPASS or at a county assistance office. Once financially eligible, the person is enrolled with one of the three CHC managed care organizations in their zone, which coordinates their long-term services and supports.
unique_feature: CHC is mandatory managed care: rather than a standalone waiver you enroll in, long-term services and supports are delivered through an MCO that also coordinates your physical health care, so one plan covers both.

administered_by: the Maryland Department of Health Medicaid Administration, with access coordinated through Maryland Access Point
eligibility_threshold: Maryland does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. Applicants must be 18 or older, need a nursing facility level of care, live at home or in the community, and not be enrolled in another waiver or PACE at the same time.
asset_limit_single: $2,000 or $2,500 in countable assets, depending on eligibility category
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited page; spousal rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: Call Maryland Access Point at 844-627-5465 to be added to the Community Options Waiver Registry, then wait for an invitation to apply. People already in a nursing facility with 30 or more days of Medicaid-paid services can apply without waiting on the registry.
unique_feature: Maryland runs the waiver from a registry with a waitlist rather than open enrollment, so getting on the Maryland Access Point list early matters - except for people already in a nursing facility, who bypass the wait entirely.

program_full_name: Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for persons who are Elderly, Blind, or Disabled
administered_by: the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing, with level-of-care determinations made annually by local Case Management Agencies
eligibility_threshold: Colorado does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. Applicants 65 and older must be determined to have a significant functional impairment; those 18 to 64 must be blind, physically disabled, or have an HIV or AIDS diagnosis. All must need long-term support at a level comparable to a nursing facility.
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: A local Case Management Agency determines level of care and reviews it annually. All waiver services need prior approval before Health First Colorado will pay for them.
unique_feature: The EBD waiver includes Consumer Directed Attendant Support Services (CDASS), which lets families direct and hire their own attendant care rather than being assigned an agency, alongside In Home Support Services and adult day health.

program_full_name: Family Care (with IRIS as the self-directed alternative)
administered_by: the Wisconsin Department of Health Services, through Aging and Disability Resource Centers for eligibility and managed care organizations for services
eligibility_threshold: Wisconsin does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. Applicants must be 18 or older, be a frail elder or an adult with a disability, be eligible for Wisconsin Medicaid, and be found functionally eligible through the Long-Term Care Functional Screen, which an ADRC screener completes in a face-to-face interview.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the cited page; set by Wisconsin Medicaid financial eligibility rules
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited page; spousal rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: Contact the local Aging and Disability Resource Center, which explains the program and completes the Long-Term Care Functional Screen. Once eligible, the member chooses a managed care organization serving their county and enrolls.
unique_feature: Wisconsin offers a genuine choice of delivery model: Family Care, where an MCO coordinates services, or IRIS (Include, Respect, I Self-Direct), where the participant self-directs their own budget and hires their own workers.

program_full_name: Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults
administered_by: NC Medicaid, within the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services, through local case management entities
eligibility_threshold: North Carolina does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. CAP/DA is for adults 18 and older who are at risk of institutionalization and who meet a nursing facility level of care, where no household member, relative, caregiver or other party is able or willing to meet all of the person's medical, psychosocial and functional needs.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the cited page; set by NC Medicaid financial eligibility rules
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited page; spousal rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: A referral goes to the local CAP/DA case management entity, which assesses medical, functional and financial eligibility. There has been a waitlist for the program.
unique_feature: CAP/Choice is North Carolina's self-directed option within CAP/DA, adding a care advisor, a personal assistant the family selects, and financial management services on top of the standard menu of adult day health, personal care aide and respite.
